about: Heat-relevant announcements from the first days of COP31 (check-in 1 of 4, 12 November 2026), found through press coverage and then tied to primary pages: WHO, UN News, IFRC, UNEP and WMO. A claim passes only when one route holds all its terms. Items that are not about heat, or are statements rather than commitments, are left out (see about-set-aside).

claims.text: COP31 opened with the launch of the Antalya Initiative, a voluntary platform for countries to share their experience of making health systems resilient to climate risks.
On the launch day no country had yet announced that it would take part.
A joint initiative with WHO brings climate information into public health planning: a forecast of dangerously high temperatures, for example, can help hospitals prepare for more patients.

The COP31 presidency's action agenda includes a theme on Dynamic and Resilient Health Systems, which prioritises health systems that can anticipate, respond to and recover from climate-related shocks through preparedness, surveillance and resilient infrastructure. Unlike many other themes, it carries no numerical target for 2035.
IFRC's call to action for COP31 notes that only 35% of countries have reported having health early warning systems for heat-related illness.

claims.where: Signals: COP31 watch (cooling and heat plans)
claims.text: IFRC's call to action for COP31 asks for investment in multi-sector local action for cities and communities to reduce heat risk, from heat action plans and early warning to shock-responsive social protection and nature-based solutions.
UNEP's Adaptation Gap Report 2026 estimates that developing countries need about US$305 billion a year for adaptation by 2035.
International public adaptation finance to developing countries was about US$28 to 32 billion in 2024.
Even if the COP30 aim of tripling international public adaptation finance is met, it would cover only about 20 to 29% of needs.
The Extreme Heat Risk Governance Framework and Toolkit is being piloted in 2026 in Barbados, Senegal and Cambodia.

about-set-aside: Global Cooling Pledge and its Intergovernmental Committee on Cooling: agreed at COP30, not a COP31 outcome; context only.
A statement by the UN climate chief that the climate crisis is a health emergency: a statement, not a commitment, and it names an individual.
Pre-COP31 civil society statements on heat action plans: communities' calls, not commitments by governments.
